subject: Vector API latency spike after model metadata push
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@marketlytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: support@marketlytics.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden Vector API slowdown — started ~08:30 PDT

Hi Marcus,

We started seeing a big jump in latency on your /v1/vectorize endpoint around 08:30 PDT this morning. p95 went from ~120ms to ~1.4s and p99 is up to ~3.6s. This started shortly after our daily job that calls embeddings for search indexing. No other infra changes on our side that we can see.

Attached is a screenshot from our monitoring dashboard and a short HAR from a failing request. Can you confirm if Redwood did anything in the last hour (catalog update, model promotion, or config change)? This is impacting our nightly index job and causing timeouts.

Thanks — we’re trying to avoid a full reindex tonight.

— Elena
Elena Ramos
Head of Search Engineering, MarketLytics
(elena.ramos@marketlytics.com)

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the screenshots. Really sorry for the disruption. We saw concurrent alerts from our hosted clusters and I’m escalating to SRE and Product to triage immediately.

Quick notes:
- Have you seen increased QPS or any change in payload size?
- Can you share a sample request ID (X-Request-ID) if available?

Next steps from our side: Rishi will pull perf snapshots and check whether the model catalog promotion that ran at 08:18 PDT touched variants used by your account. We’ll circle back in 30–45m with an initial triage. If needed we’ll roll back the promotion or route your traffic to the previous model variant.

I’ll keep you updated here.

— Marcus

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@marketlytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden Vector API slowdown — started ~08:30 PDT

Marcus / team — initial triage: we confirm a p95/p99 regression on the public vector pools that correlates with a model-catalog metadata promotion at 08:18 PDT (deploy tag: catalog-promo-20270418). The promotion changed a default routing policy for one of the embeddings models which caused a small percentage of traffic to be routed to a variant that has a different attention kernel path.

What we see in perf_snapshot_20270418.json (attached):
- Median latency unchanged for most clusters (~110ms)
- p95 increased from 120ms to 1.4s for the affected pool
- p99 spikes up to 3.6s due to a small set of requests hitting a slower kernel path when seq_len > 1024 and kv-cache warmup occurs
- No obvious memory pressure or GPU throttling; CPU scheduling jitter observed on aggregator nodes during the catalog sync window

Immediate mitigations executed (09:40 PDT):
1) Rolled back the routing change for the affected model variant for customer-tagged traffic.
2) Enabled temporary prefix-KV pinning for MarketLytics to avoid cold kv-cache misses.
3) Opened INF-2893 for a full root-cause follow-up (link below).

Rishi
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: perf_snapshot_20270418.json (application/json)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Executive brief: MarketLytics vector latency regression and containment

Naomi — FYI and request for exec-level awareness. Customer MarketLytics (mid-enterprise, search product) experienced a p95/p99 regression spanning ~08:30–09:40 PDT after a model-catalog metadata promotion. Rishi rolled back routing changes and applied temporary KV pinning for the account; status is now stabilized but we need an RCA and a customer-facing summary.

Impact:
- Customer nightly index job timed out and retried; they deferred a full reindex (risk to renewal conversation if this repeats)
- Incident classification: Sev 2 (targeting SLA breach risk)

Ask: please approve outreach to offer two weeks of compute credits and a short technical review session with their engineering leadership. We may also want to loop in Legal if they request contract-level remediation.

Evelyn
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@marketlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden Vector API slowdown — started ~08:30 PDT

Hi Elena — following up with a summary and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption. Short version: a catalog metadata promotion changed the default routing for one embeddings variant which exposed a slower kernel path for long-sequence requests. Our SREs rolled back the routing change and enabled KV pinning for your account; your p95/p99 numbers returned to normal within ~30m after rollback.

What we’ve done for you:
- Full incident log and perf snapshot attached.
- Two weeks of compute credits for your account (applied today).
- Scheduled a 60-minute technical session next Tues to review best practices for sequence-length handling and catalog pinning.

We’re tracking follow-ups in INF-2893 and will provide the RCA doc when complete. If you prefer, I can connect you directly with Rishi and our runtime lead during the session.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll continue monitoring your telemetry and will notify you of any related changes well in advance.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
